motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming September 2024 as Parent Teacher…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming September 2024 as Parent Teacher Association Membership Month, as read by Mayor Westmoreland. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: September named PTA Membership Month
motions.summary: The council proclaimed September 2024 as Parent Teacher Association Membership Month.
motions.impact: Purely symbolic — nothing changes for residents. It is an encouragement to join your school's PTA, with no money, fees, or rules attached.

motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing item 13.C. A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with Stephen Mumford for Interim City Manager Services, and amending item 10.A. Agreement Renewal – Legislative Executive Consulting, LLC to a two-year extension. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items passed; interim manager deal pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, but pulled out the interim city manager agreement with Stephen Mumford and extended a legislative consulting contract to two years.
motions.impact: Mostly routine housekeeping with no effect on residents. The notable part is what did not pass: the interim city manager contract was removed from the batch rather than approved with it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving the Towns at Brylee Farms Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving the Towns at Brylee Farms Development Agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay decision on Towns at Brylee Farms
motions.summary: The council set aside the development agreement for Towns at Brylee Farms without deciding it.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled for this project. If you are following Brylee Farms, the agreement has to come back on a future agenda before anything moves.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Tract Development Agreement. City Attorney Marcus Draper presented the item. The proposed ordinance approves the Tract Development Agreement, which covers approximately 672 acres of land distributed among 2 different parcels. One of the parcels is located near the Meta, Google, and QTS sites. The other parcel abuts Industrial Planning Area 2 of the Firefly development in the southwestern portion of the City. Applicant representative Keely Ambrose addressed the Council regarding concerns around buffering, the addition of property, benchmarks, and length of the agreement. Eagle Mountain City Council Emergency Meeting – August 20, 2024 Page 6 of 9
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Tract Development Agreement with the following change: 1. The last three sentences in Section 4.12 are removed and replaced with, “If Additional Property is annexed into this Agreement pursuant to this Section 4.12, then such future property shall be buffered as required by the Applicable Rules. This paragraph does not apply to any property located outside the City limits unless it is annexed into the City.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 672-acre development deal near the data centers
motions.summary: The council took up a development agreement covering roughly 672 acres in two parcels — one near the Meta, Google and QTS sites, one next to Firefly.
motions.impact: The land sits by the data centers and the Firefly area in the southwest, not in existing neighborhoods. The change discussed would require buffering for any land added to the deal later, and only once it is inside city limits.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Economic Development Director Evan Berrett presented the item. The proposed ordinance will allow for the creation of the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area. This Plan is the end result of a comprehensive evaluation of the types of appropriate land uses and economic development for the land, which lies within twenty-four parcels in the City. The north parcels are south of 4000 North, north of Pole Canyon Blvd, and east of Tyson Pkwy. The south parcel is south of 1000 North and east of Pony Express Pkwy. The Plan is intended to define the method and means of the Project Area from its current state to a higher and better use.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Adopt Triple Tail redevelopment plan for 24 parcels
motions.summary: The council adopted a redevelopment plan for the Triple Tail area — 24 parcels near Pole Canyon Blvd and east of Pony Express Pkwy — to steer them toward higher-value uses.
motions.impact: If you live near those parcels, this sets the city's blueprint for the kinds of development it wants there. Nothing is built yet; the plan is the roadmap, not a project.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Consulting Services for the Downtown Master Plan. The proposed resolution approves an agreement for consulting services for the Downtown Master Plan. The City Council received presentations from three firms in the earlier work session and selected their preferred firm during this scheduled item.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Consulting Services with MHTN Architects for the Downtown Master Plan. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hire MHTN Architects to plan a downtown
motions.summary: The city hired MHTN Architects to write the Downtown Master Plan, picking the firm from three that pitched the council earlier that night.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This is the planning stage — a consultant will draft what a downtown could look like, and any real construction would come much later.

motions.item_title: Remove the “MIHP regarding Impact Fees for ADUs” item from the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to remove the “MIHP regarding Impact Fees for ADUs” item from the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Drop ADU impact-fee item from lobbying list
motions.summary: The council removed a proposal about impact fees for accessory dwelling units from the list of issues it asks state lawmakers to act on.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. It only trims what the city lobbies the Legislature about; no fee or rule in Eagle Mountain changed.
